lines.text: To a samurai, surrendering meant spiritual deathâ€”their razor-sharp katana was revered as the living vessel of their very soul.
Master swordsmiths folded iron sand twenty times, forging weapons capable of cleaving armor with terrifying elegance.
Bound by Bushidoâ€”the Way of the Warriorâ€”they lived by seven sacred virtues: courage, respect, and unflinching loyalty.
During the brutal Sengoku civil wars, massive armies clashed with spears, bows, and matchlock muskets to unite Japan.
Legendary duelists like Miyamoto Musashi mastered the blade not merely to kill, but to attain supreme inner enlightenment.
Though their era ended, the indomitable warrior spirit echoes forever. Subscribe to Beyond History for more.
